text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Vietnam's Communist Party marked its 67th anniversary with a meeting in Hanoi on Sunday.
-- Foreign law firms in Vietnam will be subject to taxation in accordance with new Justice Ministry regulations.
-- Vietnam plans to export at least 2.6 million tonnes of rice this year, despite recent prolonged flooding in the Mekong Delta.
-- The government has instructed ministries and local authorities to offer help to poor families threatened by hunger ahead of the traditional Tet Lunar New Year.
-- Provinces and cities throughout the country have held meetings to celebrate the 67th-anniversary of the Communist Party.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has asked media to step up efforts to combat incorrect implementation of Party and government policies, and criticise distortions of government policy by hostile forces.
-- Vietnam's industrial output rose by 12.9 percent in January over the same period last year.
-- Vietnam's crude oil output reached 814,000 tonnes in January.
-- More than 2,700 people joined the Communist Party in Ho Chi Minh City in 1996
